PREPLANNING_CONTEXT: {"version":1,"schema_version":2,"epicId":"d63f-2c74","generatedAt":"2026-06-02T00:00:00Z","generatedBy":"preplanning","epic":{"title":"[brainstorm/preplanning]: operational atomicity check — detect artifact-reference desync patterns in AC generation","description":"Category 8 red-team taxonomy + ast-grep-required + bootstrap pair-discovery migration + antipattern registry + config-key doc sub-task + refresh command.","successCriteria":["sc-1","sc-2","sc-3","sc-4","sc-5","sc-6","sc-7","sc-8"]},"researchFindings":[],"stories":[{"id":"f93d-7989-5bf5-456c","title":"As a DSO operator, I want ast-grep enforced as a required onboarding dependency with shadow-utils disambiguation, so that the atomicity check never runs against the wrong binary.","description":"## Description
**What**: Reclassify ast-grep from optional to required in onboarding/SKILL.md and INSTALL.md, add an identity-probe dependency check that hard-exits non-zero when ast-grep is absent or when the only sg on PATH is the Linux shadow-utils setgid /usr/bin/sg, and convert all DSO scripts to invoke the long-form ast-grep binary.
**Why**: A bare command -v sg can resolve to the shadow-utils newgrp tool, silently running the wrong binary and defeating every downstream ast-grep consumer.
**Scope**:
- IN: identity probe parsing sg --version and accepting only ast-grep >= 0.20; hard-exit non-zero with an error naming ast-grep plus a recommended install command (cargo/npm/brew); onboarding/SKILL.md and INSTALL.md required-dependency + shadow-utils collision docs; conversion of DSO script call sites to the long-form binary.
- OUT: /dso:doctor changes; CI precondition wiring.","priority":1,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":true,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["An onboarding run with ast-grep absent and a decoy setgid sg on PATH exits non-zero and the error output contains the string ast-grep and a recommended install command ← Satisfies: sc-2","The identity probe parses sg --version and rejects any sg that is not ast-grep at version 0.20 or greater ← Satisfies: sc-2","onboarding/SKILL.md and INSTALL.md list ast-grep as required with minimum version 0.20, cargo/npm/brew install instructions, and the /usr/bin/sg shadow-utils collision note ← Validates Closure Check: "onboarding docs list ast-grep as required (minimum version >= 0.20) with install instructions (cargo/npm/brew) and document the /usr/bin/sg shadow-utils collision."","Every DSO script that invokes structural search calls the long-form ast-grep binary rather than the bare sg alias ← Satisfies: sc-2","Unit tests written and passing for the identity probe across the absent, decoy-shadow, and valid-ast-grep cases ← Satisfies: sc-2"],"considerations":["[Build] New .sh files set the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation.","[Coordination] onboarding/SKILL.md is shared with the Java onboarding epic (70d5); coordinate hard-exit semantics to avoid divergent exit-code contracts.","[Risk] Onboarding hard-exit does not propagate to CI; note a follow-up to add a CI ast-grep precondition before planning jobs (out of this story's scope)."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":[],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-2"},{"id":"a63e-0acd-3cd4-4a04","title":"As a DSO planner, I want implementation-plan to emit a paired config-key documentation sub-task, so that every config-key change updates CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md atomically.","description":"## Description
**What**: Update implementation-plan/SKILL.md so that for any task adding, modifying, or removing a dso-config.conf key it emits a separate child sub-task (testing_mode GREEN) titled 'Document <key> in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md' carrying a depends_on link to the parent task, superseding the generic doc-router path for config keys.
**Why**: This is the same artifact-desync pattern that motivated the epic (release.sh + marketplace.json); a config key and its reference doc must update together.
**Scope**:
- IN: add/modify/remove key detection in implementation-plan/SKILL.md; child sub-task emission with depends_on to the parent; suppression of the duplicate generic doc-router documentation task for config keys.
- OUT: the inference-gate config key itself (draft-6); reviewer Category 8 pass.","priority":1,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["An implementation-plan run on a task that adds a dso-config.conf key yields a child sub-task titled Document <key> in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md whose depends_on points to the parent task id ← Satisfies: sc-4","An implementation-plan run on a task that modifies or removes a dso-config.conf key yields the same paired documentation child sub-task ← Satisfies: sc-4","For a config-key task the generic doc-router documentation task is not emitted, so no duplicate documentation task exists ← Satisfies: sc-4","The emitted child sub-task carries testing_mode GREEN ← Satisfies: sc-4"],"considerations":["[Sequencing] This story is sequenced before the inference-gate story (draft-6) so SC8's key documentation follows the established config-key/doc pairing pattern.","[Coordination] CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md is edited at story-run time across many config-adding epics; coordinate key namespacing rather than locking the file at epic-merge time."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":[],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-4"},{"id":"493d-8cf0-5aa7-4561","title":"As a DSO maintainer, I want a bootstrap migration that discovers writer/reference artifact pairs into a seed registry, so that planning has an authoritative coupling list.","description":"## Description
**What**: Build the walking-skeleton path: a shared normalize-and-sort registry library, a plugin-shipped seed registry of artifact-reference pairs, and a bootstrap migration script that fans out ast-grep over chunked codebase slices (map) and equijoins per-file tuples on the realpath-normalized path (reduce) to emit admitted writer/reference pairs.
**Why**: Without a deterministic discovered registry there is nothing for the Category 8 reviewer pass or the refresh command to consume; this is the minimal 'pairs discovered into a registry' spine.
**Scope**:
- IN: shared normalize-and-sort library file sourced by the bootstrap; seed registry YAML shipping the three named pairs; bootstrap map/reduce script using long-form ast-grep; write-idiom vocabulary (shell >/>>, tee, sed -i, jq write, Python open(w)/Path.write_text, Node fs.writeFileSync, Ruby File.open(w)/File.write, Go os.WriteFile) externally extensible via registry config; admission rule (exact realpath match + recognized write idiom + writer and reference in different files).
- OUT: refresh command (draft-3); reviewer consumption (draft-5); ambiguous/inferred pairs.","priority":0,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":true,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pair release.sh paired with marketplace.json ← Validates Closure Check: "The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pairs release.sh<->marketplace.json, *.conf<->CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and plugin.json<->marketplace source ref."","The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pair *.conf paired with CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md and the pair plugin.json paired with the marketplace source ref ← Validates Closure Check: "The plugin-shipped seed registry contains the pairs release.sh<->marketplace.json, *.conf<->CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and plugin.json<->marketplace source ref."","The shared normalize-and-sort registry library file exists and the bootstrap script sources it ← Validates Closure Check: "The shared normalize-and-sort registry library file exists and is sourced by both the bootstrap and refresh scripts."","Running the bootstrap over a fixture repo emits output byte-equal to a sorted newline-delimited writer_realpath<TAB>reference_realpath manifest with no missing or extra rows; near-miss fixtures (same-file self-reference; cross-file read-only) are absent from the output ← Satisfies: sc-3","Unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic including the realpath-normalized equijoin, write-idiom recognition, and near-miss rejection ← Satisfies: sc-3"],"considerations":["[Build] New .sh files set the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation; the test gate and pre-commit hooks skip non-executable .sh files.","[Correctness] All ast-grep invocations use the long-form ast-grep binary, never the bare sg alias, to avoid the shadow-utils collision.","[Risk] Bootstrap sub-agents can truncate tuple lists at context limit silently; emit a per-slice count and fail the reduce when a slice returns no tuples unexpectedly.","[Determinism] The shared library performs idempotent sort-dedup so bootstrap and refresh share identical normalization."],"scopeSplitCandidate":true,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["f93d-7989-5bf5-456c"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-3"},{"id":"7cf1-ff9d-ddfb-4074","title":"As a DSO maintainer, I want a re-runnable registry-refresh command that detects newly-added writer/reference pairs, so that the registry does not go stale after the one-time bootstrap.","description":"## Description
**What**: Add a re-runnable registry-refresh command that shares the normalize-and-sort library with the bootstrap, applies idempotent sort-dedup on write, and surfaces writer/reference pairs added since the last run.
**Why**: The bootstrap is one-time; without refresh the registry drifts from the codebase and the atomicity check misses new couplings.
**Scope**:
- IN: refresh command sourcing the shared normalize-and-sort library; idempotent sort-dedup on write; detection of pairs added since the last run; no-change re-run surfaces nothing.
- OUT: bootstrap discovery internals (draft-1); reviewer consumption.","priority":2,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["A refresh re-run on a fixture repo with exactly one newly-added writer/reference pair surfaces exactly that pair as an update candidate ← Satisfies: sc-7","A refresh re-run on an unchanged fixture repo surfaces no update candidates ← Satisfies: sc-7","The refresh command sources the shared normalize-and-sort registry library used by the bootstrap ← Validates Closure Check: "The shared normalize-and-sort registry library file exists and is sourced by both the bootstrap and refresh scripts."","Writing the refreshed registry twice with no intervening change produces a byte-identical file (idempotent sort-dedup) ← Satisfies: sc-7","Unit tests written and passing for the added-pair detection and idempotent-write logic ← Satisfies: sc-7"],"considerations":["[Build] New .sh files set the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation.","[Determinism] Reuse the shared library's sort-dedup so refresh and bootstrap emit identically-ordered registries; do not re-implement normalization."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["493d-8cf0-5aa7-4561"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-7"},{"id":"d146-d258-7359-4794","title":"As a story-map reviewer, I want a Category 8 atomicity pass that reads the registry and emits co-update findings with deferred-coordination handling, so that artifact-reference desync is caught before implementation.","description":"## Description
**What**: Add Category 8 'Operational Atomicity / Artifact-Reference Desync' to the red-team-reviewer story_review taxonomy and add operational_atomicity to the taxonomy_category enum; the pass reads the antipattern registry at registry.antipattern_path (injected via dispatch arguments), emits a registry-backed authoritative finding whose AC names the paired referencing file and requires atomic same-commit update, injects a pre-emptive audit task from a matching file_class audit_task_template, and degrades gracefully when the registry is absent or unparseable. When a registered referencing file is not co-updatable in the same commit, the finding instead emits a deferred-coordination note recorded as a story consideration.
**Why**: This is the consumption point that turns the discovered registry into planning-time findings that prevent the desync.
**Scope**:
- IN: Category 8 taxonomy + enum value; registry read at registry.antipattern_path injected via dispatch arguments with absent and unparseable diagnostics; registry-backed finding naming the paired referencing file; audit-task injection from audit_task_template; Cat 8 suppresses parallel Cat 6 for the same pair; rename/remove cases defer to Cat 7; SC6 non-co-updatable classification (git check-ignore, is_generated_file(), cross-repo URL, branch-protection) emitting a deferred-coordination consideration and follow-up task.
- OUT: the LLM-inference pass and its config gate (draft-6).","priority":2,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["A preplanning run over a fixture story editing a registered writer emits a finding with taxonomy_category operational_atomicity and an AC string naming the paired referencing file ← Satisfies: sc-1","The Category 8 pass receives the registry path from the orchestrator dispatch arguments at registry.antipattern_path and does not self-discover or hardcode the path; a dispatch with no registry argument produces the registry-absent diagnostic rather than a fallback file lookup ← Satisfies: sc-1","The red-team-reviewer.md taxonomy_category enum includes the value operational_atomicity ← Validates Closure Check: "red-team-reviewer.md taxonomy_category enum includes the value operational_atomicity."","A Category 8 finding suppresses a parallel Category 6 finding for the same writer/reference pair; rename or remove cases defer to Category 7 ← Satisfies: sc-1","With the registry absent the pass completes and logs registry absent; with a corrupt fixture the pass completes and logs registry unreadable as a distinct message; with a valid fixture a matching file_class injects the audit task from audit_task_template ← Satisfies: sc-5","A generated-file fixture yields a deferred-coordination consideration and a follow-up coordination task rather than a hard atomic-update AC ← Satisfies: sc-6","Unit tests written and passing for the registry-read diagnostics, the dispatch-arg injection path, the operational_atomicity finding emission, the Cat 6 suppression, and the SC6 non-co-updatable classification ← Satisfies: sc-1"],"considerations":["[Dependency] The SC5 registry schema may be shipped by clear-fairy (7575-5a90); if it is not yet available, a local fixture registry supplies the {file_class, pattern, audit_task_template} + schema_version shape. Do not own migration code for clear-fairy's final schema; adaptation is limited to updating registry.antipattern_path and schema_version.","[Build] New .sh files set the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation.","[Correctness] The registry is injected via orchestrator dispatch arguments at registry.antipattern_path, not discovered by the reviewer itself.","[Risk] Branch-protection lookups via gh api treat a 404 as not-protected and cache the result per-branch to avoid repeated API calls."],"scopeSplitCandidate":true,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["493d-8cf0-5aa7-4561","a63e-0acd-3cd4-4a04"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-1;sc-5;sc-6"},{"id":"5078-537c-42a1-40b5","title":"As a DSO operator, I want a config key that gates only the Category 8 LLM-inference pass, so that non-deterministic advisory findings can be disabled while registry findings always run.","description":"## Description
**What**: Add the config key review.atomicity_inference_enabled (default false), documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, that gates only the Category 8 LLM-inference pass; the deterministic registry pass always runs. LLM-inferred findings carry confidence: advisory.
**Why**: The inference pass fires non-deterministically across runs; a toggle plus advisory confidence keeps the deterministic registry authoritative while letting operators disable inference.
**Scope**:
- IN: review.atomicity_inference_enabled key (default false); the LLM-inference pass emitting confidence: advisory findings gated by the key; CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md documentation of this key and registry.antipattern_path.
- OUT: the deterministic registry pass (draft-5), which always runs regardless of this key.","priority":3,"classification":"new","walkingSkeleton":false,"hasWireframe":false,"doneDefinitions":["With review.atomicity_inference_enabled false a planning run emits zero confidence advisory findings but still emits registry-backed findings ← Satisfies: sc-8","With review.atomicity_inference_enabled true the LLM-inference pass emits findings carrying confidence advisory ← Satisfies: sc-8","review.atomicity_inference_enabled and registry.antipattern_path are documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md with description, type, default, and scope ← Validates Closure Check: "review.atomicity_inference_enabled and registry.antipattern_path are documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md."","Unit tests written and passing for the gated inference pass in both the key-false and key-true states ← Satisfies: sc-8"],"considerations":["[Sequencing] This story depends on the SC4 paired-doc story (draft-4) so the key documentation follows the established config-key/doc pairing pattern, and on draft-5 which owns the deterministic registry pass this key sits beside.","[Build] New .sh files set the executable bit (chmod +x) on creation."],"scopeSplitCandidate":false,"splitRole":null,"splitPairId":null,"blockedBy":["a63e-0acd-3cd4-4a04","d146-d258-7359-4794"],"satisfiesCriterion":"sc-8"}],"storyDashboard":{"totalStories":6,"uiStories":0,"criticalPath":["f93d-7989-5bf5-456c","493d-8cf0-5aa7-4561","d146-d258-7359-4794"]}}
